sammendrag: A National Basic Skills Programme was implemented by the Employment Service (now Jobcentre Plus) in April 2001. Under this programme, jobseekers who had been unemployed for at least 6 months or were entering New Deal were screened for a basic skills need. If a need is confirmed, the customer would then be referred onto a basic skills training course. In order to explore the impact of sanctions on the people taking up and completing basic skills training more thoroughly, an extended 12 month Mandatory Training Pilot scheme was introduced in April 2004. This report presents findings from stages 1 and 2 of the 5-stage evaluation. The report explores the implementation and delivery of recent National Enhancements to the Basic Skills Programme. It also focuses on the views and attitudes of customers, Jobcentre Plus staff, and providers regarding the impact of sanctions and incentives on participation in the basic skills process.
tittel: Evaluation of Basic Skills Mandatory Training Pilot and National Enhancements: interim report
